claims.text: Morgan Stanley is investing in technology for its advisors through ongoing investments in its world-class platform to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and expansion of its workplace channel, alongside continued investment in future technology including AI and digital tools.

Morgan Stanley names among its early AI use cases LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform for matching workplace and self-directed relationships and engaging financial advisors, Parable, an interactive data-analysis tool, and the DevGen AI code-modernization tool (3Q25), and says it was overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth including work with OpenAI (3Q26).

It also cites continued investment in deepening its competitive moats through an expanded Carta collaboration in private markets and announced Zero Hash partnerships in digital assets (3Q25), and significant resources toward digital tools, digital enhancements, and automation for lending products (1Q26).

It attributes insights from its size and scale that let financial advisors tailor advice and equip its own tools (3Q26), continues to invest across its technology stack embracing AI tools (3Q26), and has been investing in its processes and systems to better understand its data and better service its clients (4Q24).

Specific tools and capabilities include LeadIQ to match individuals with advisers (2Q26), AI 'co-piloting' with 'corridors' or 'super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio (1Q26), and, in CEO Ted Pick's words, using scale to invest in broadening financial-advisor capabilities—alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending (4Q25).

AI and automation initiatives directed at advisors include LeadIQ for matching workplace and self-directed relationships and engaging financial advisors (as of 2025-09-30), 'co-piloting' with 'corridors' or 'super agents' under Jed Finn and Andy Saperstein (as of 2026-03-31), technology to improve automation and facilitate client acquisition openings plus increased advisor and client education (as of 2025-12-31), and ongoing investments in automation and AI while assessing where its people should be over the next five to ten years (as of 2025-03-31).

CEO Edward Pick describes AI as a top priority for the firm's advisory role and says it is existentially important that Morgan Stanley be viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem, and he frames 'world-class technology, world-class cyber defense' combined with the best trusted advisers sitting with the client as the 'secret sauce.'

He also states technology can help do a lot of the early work for financial advisers around protecting client assets and a resiliency theme, that cyber resiliency is a top priority across all businesses with AI bringing efficiency and effectiveness, and that the firm has built advantages making technology a differentiator in its favor.

CEO Ted Pick says the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology with growth plans embedding increasing AI adoption, and describes the early digital asset transformation in wealth—a Zero Hash partnership, crypto and tokenized asset capabilities, and continued E*TRADE work.

CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology including AI and digital tools, and that the firm continues to invest across its technology stack embracing AI tools.
